subject: ACCEPT statement
notes: 'The implementor shall specify the device that is used if the FROM phrase is not specified.' BindAccept: `if (ac.acceptSource() is not { } src) return new BoundAccept(target, AcceptKind.Device) ...` with the inline citation '// GR5 -- FROM omitted: the implementor default (stdin)'; the emitter then routes it to AcceptSource.Device, which reads Console.In, i.e. the process standard input. The specification is also DOCUMENTED as the rule's Annex A.1 item 2 requires (required + documented): docs/CONFORMANCE.md's A.1 determination table carries the row 'ACCEPT statement -- device used when FROM is unspecified, 14.9.1 GR5, required + documented ... the process standard input stream', and `python scripts/spec/audit_annex_a1.py --check` confirms the row matches item 2's element ('FINDINGS: none -- every section 7 row names an A.1 item whose element it matches'). This is the ONE ACCEPT A.1 obligation that is discharged (items 1 and 5 are not -- see GR-14.9.1.4-1 and -2). Verified end-to-end by every bare-`ACCEPT WS-X.` case in AcceptDifferentialTests, which pipe stdin and read back the stored value. || UPHELD: re-read AcceptDisplayBinder.cs:62-63 -- the early return really is unconditional on `ac.acceptSource()` being absent, so no source shape can reach a different default, and AcceptSource.Device's only input is `Console.In.ReadLine()` (AcceptSource.cs:89). The two cited tests both compile a bare `ACCEPT WS-X.` and pipe stdin, so they do exercise the FROM-omitted default rather than a mnemonic path. GR5 has one half (specify a device) and it is both implemented and documented; CONFORMS is correct.
